original_question:
Let f̂ denote the Fourier transform of f. Let H2(R) = { f ∈ L2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0 }. Let ψ ∈ L2(R), and define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for H2(R) if the wavelet system {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of H2(R).

Does there exist a Riesz wavelet ψ in H2(R) such that ψ belongs to the Schwartz class?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Problem 2.2: "Does there exist a Riesz wavelet ψ in H^2(R) such that ψ belongs to the Schwartz class?" ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it uses the Hardy space H^2(R) = {f ∈ L^2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0}, the classical dyadic affine system ψ_{j,k}(x) = 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), and the correct notion that a Riesz wavelet for H^2(R) means this system is a Riesz basis of H^2(R). The final existence question about Schwartz regularity is essentially the paper's Problem 2.2. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully paper-faithful, it helps to say explicitly that this is the classical one-dimensional dyadic wavelet setting from Definition 2.1 and equation (2.1), not a more general dilation/lattice setting. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The paper's shorthand "a Riesz wavelet ψ in H^2(R)" implicitly means ψ ∈ H^2(R); your draft starts with ψ ∈ L^2(R), which is harmless once the basis property is imposed, but slightly less explicit than the paper's phrasing. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

For complete stand-alone wording, one can spell out that "Schwartz class" means the Schwartz class S(R) on the real line. This is implicit in the paper. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The nearby context matters: Theorem 2.7 rules out orthonormal wavelets in H^2(R) with the regularity assumptions of Theorem 2.6, and hence rules out Schwartz-class orthonormal wavelets there; the open problem is specifically about general Riesz wavelets, not the orthonormal case. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The paper also notes that Auscher's work excludes the biorthogonal Riesz-wavelet case, so the intended open problem is the remaining general Riesz-wavelet case beyond biorthogonal wavelets. Your draft does not mention this boundary, though it does not incorrectly broaden the problem. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
refined_question: In the classical one-dimensional dyadic setting, let H^2(R) = {f ∈ L^2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0}. Does there exist a function ψ ∈ S(R) ∩ H^2(R) such that the affine system {2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k) : j, k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of H^2(R)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent by the paper's definition of a Riesz wavelet for H^2(R): Does there exist a Riesz wavelet ψ in H^2(R) such that ψ belongs to the Schwartz class? ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the exact target. The paper first defines the dyadic wavelet system in Definition 2.1, then in §2.2 defines H^2(R), recalls Auscher's negative result for orthonormal wavelets in H^2(R) with the regularity assumptions of Theorem 2.6, states in Theorem 2.7 that in particular there is no Schwartz-class orthonormal wavelet basis for H^2(R), and immediately says that this leaves open Seip's problem, formulated as Problem 2.2. The refined question above keeps precisely that scope and only makes explicit the dyadic setting and the membership ψ ∈ H^2(R) ∩ S(R). It does not broaden the problem to biorthogonal wavelets, other dilations, other lattices, or other function classes. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
